paragraphs.text: Lancaster III JA964, marked MG-P, took off from Oakington at 18:58 on 22 March 1944 to bomb Frankfurt. It flew with 7 Squadron, 8 Group. The raid that night involved 816 aircraft, and 33 were lost. Nothing was heard from JA964 after take-off, and it did not return.

Post-war enquiries established that the aircraft had been shot down. The memorial in Longstanton says a night fighter did it. The pilot, Flying Officer Kenneth Hinde, said in 1945 that the Lancaster was attacked ten minutes before the target and again two minutes later, which set the port inner engine on fire. He ordered the crew out at about 16,000 feet and put the crash half way between Frankfurt and Saarbrucken. The bomb aimer, Flight Sergeant Harry McMaster, said he baled out at 19,000 feet with the controls useless and a fire in the port engine. He put the crash 10 miles east of a place he gave as 'Jaoberstein', east of Trier. The two accounts place the crash in different spots, and no source here settles which is right.

Four men died: Flying Officer John Henry Wyborn (navigator, 28), Flight Sergeant Jack Lambert (wireless operator/air gunner, 22, RAAF), Flight Sergeant Gordon Eben Hamilton (rear gunner, 20, RNZAF) and Sergeant Albert Edward Bullivant (mid-upper gunner, 20). All four are buried at Rheinberg War Cemetery. Three survived as prisoners of war: Hinde, Sergeant Albert Ivon Love (flight engineer) and McMaster. Hinde and McMaster were released by the Russians.

The memorial is a black and white photograph of aircrew in front of a Lancaster, mounted under clear plastic, with crew details in white print. It is about 125 mm high and 180 mm wide, on paper, and its condition is good. It hangs in All Saints' Church, Rampton Road, Longstanton. All Saints' is the custodian. The church is Grade I listed.

All Saints' holds the 7 Squadron Memorial Window, dedicated on 17 August 1992, and the squadron's Book of Remembrance, which lists 1,011 Second World War dead. The 7 Squadron Association holds its Remembrance Day service there each autumn. IBCC also lists a window and Roll of Honour at All Saints' in its entry for Sergeant Bullivant. The church was closed for about five years after its nave roof collapsed and reopened on 30 September 2007.

notes: CREW: our placeholder 'Unknown (PoW 1)' (Flt Sgt, Crew) is wrong. S2 names three PoWs: Hinde (pilot), Love (flight engineer, Sgt RAFVR), McMaster (bomb aimer, Flt Sgt RAAF). Love and McMaster are missing from our record; the placeholder should go, but crew names are not retracted here, so a human should remove it. Our Hinde entry says Australian; S2 gives only service RAAF, so nationality is not claimed for the PoWs. Roles for the four dead are from S2 only (IBCC just says air gunner for Bullivant). CONFLICTS/DOUBTS: (1) IWM's inscription reads 'JB455 (sic)' where the memorial text begins; our record's inscription says JA964. IBCC and S2 both give JA964 for this loss, so 'JB455' looks like an error on the stone. I did not claim the inscription field; a human should check the IWM photos. (2) IWM says 5 commemorated (1 served, 4 died); our record says 4 names and the inscription lists 4. The fifth is unidentified; the IWM page showed only a names placeholder. (3) Hinde and McMaster give different crash places (both quoted in the narrative). (4) S2 says Hinde's statement mentions only Love and McMaster as PoWs; unresolved. (5) IBCC warns the crew may not share one date of death; CWGC gives 22 March 1944 for all four. WHY IN LONGSTANTON: no source I read says who placed the photograph or when (the IWM entry gives no maker or dedication date). The 7 Squadron Association and IBCC show the church is the squadron's memorial church (window, Book of Remembrance). The IWM description says it is a 70th anniversary item (i.e. around 2014), but that rests on our own record's inscription, not an independent read. OAKINGTON/LONGSTANTON: Oakington as base is confirmed by S2 and S3. That the airfield sits beside Longstanton comes from a UK Airfields page heading ('Oakington / Longstanton / Northstowe') and a search snippet attributed to Wikipedia; neither is cited as a claim, so I left it out of the story. The 1944 Longstanton church link was not otherwise tied to this crew. NOT FOUND: IBCC pages for Wyborn, Hamilton, Lambert, Hinde, Love, McMaster (one IBCC fetch returned 429, so I stopped); Auckland Museum Cenotaph and AWM pages were not fetched; PoW camps; ages of PoWs; the target's weather or raid detail beyond IBCC. S2 is a museum tribute page and may draw on the same service files as other sources; treat its crew list as single-source for the PoWs. Lambert's Panel 125 is from S2 (AWM page not read). Coordinates untouched.
